The span's middle verse carries its densest 2ms evidence: שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ, שְׁמֶ֑ךָ, and אֲהֵבֽוּךָ (all oshb:Song.1.3, tier: byte). The addressee stays constant (2ms 'you') across the span, though בָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) is 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, left unsettled with no morphology layer staged; the grammatical person of the speaker separately shifts to the cohortative 'we' of “We will be glad and rejoice in you.” (web:Song.1.4), disclosed as texture below rather than argued as a voice-shift, since no addressee or gender-marked form changes there.

boundary_rationale: אִם לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.8, tier: byte) opens this unit: the negation sits on אִם לֹ֤א ('if not'), and תֵדְעִי֙ itself carries second-feminine-singular marking ('you know') rather than the opening token, a grammatical-gender flip from the second-masculine address of Song.1.7 that signals a new speaker. The feminine imperatives צְֽאִי and וּרְעִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.8, tier: byte, 'go out' / 'graze') hold one addressee (her); inside the span's own bytes, רַעְיָתִֽי (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte, 'my love'), his tier-1 address anchor for her (sweep: 9 verses), stands unused alongside the 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte, 'I have compared you'). The second-feminine-singular suffixes continue through לְחָיַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Song.1.10, tier: byte, 'your cheeks') and לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte, the 2fs dative in 'we will make for you'), holding one addressee across all four verses with no further gender-marked interruption: “Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.” (web:Song.1.10) and “We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.” (web:Song.1.11).

boundary_rationale: This unit's seam rests on the marked 2fs addressee dropping rather than on any replacing gender-marked first-person form: נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte, 'we will make for you'), the 2fs suffix closing the preceding unit, gives way to נִרְדִּ֖י (oshb:Song.1.12, tier: byte, 'my nard'), a gender-unmarked 1cs possessive beside the third-person עַד שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בִּמְסִבּ֔וֹ (oshb:Song.1.12, tier: byte, the melek lexeme); the shift is carried by the disappearance of the marked addressee plus tier-2 voice continuity, not by a gender-marked replacement form, and confidence is held accordingly. The dodi-exact formula anchors the rest of the run twice, דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.13, tier: byte) and דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.14, tier: byte) -- both 'my beloved is to me', her word for the man (sweep: 24 verses book-wide for the dodi-exact form). boundary_rationale: This span is held as one antiphonal bracket rather than atomized per line: הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte, 'behold you are beautiful, my love') opens in the man's voice, using his word for her in the final token; הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 'behold you are beautiful, my beloved') answers with the mirrored formula and her word for him, confirming the reply is hers, and her turn continues through קֹר֤וֹת בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ אֲרָזִ֔ים (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte, 'the beams of our house are cedars') with the 1cp form עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 'our couch') and בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte, 'our house') continuing her plural possessive with no gender-marked interruption; the verse's other 1cp noun stands as a ketiv/qere pair, ketiv רחיטנו against the qere רַהִיטֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte, 'our rafters'), disclosed here rather than claimed at either reading. Song.2.1's self-description אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת (oshb:Song.2.1, tier: byte, 'I am a rose') carries no gender-marked form and is held rather than attributed. The same mirrored alternation recurs at the far end of the span: כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, tier: byte, 'so [is] my love') is his line, and כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte, 'so [is] my beloved') is hers, closing the antiphon's second mirrored pair. The bytes run on past this close in the same first-person voice -- חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) continuing into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte) -- with no vocative, no address-vocabulary token, and no gender-marked addressee change at the cut, so the boundary at Song.2.3|Song.2.4 is not itself a voice-shift; it is held because the antiphon's own formal marker, the mirrored address pairs, completes at Song.2.2-Song.2.3, while Song.2.4 onward carries none. Confidence is held at medium_low to reflect that the closing seam is structural rather than gender-marked.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the exchange through Song.2.4-Song.2.6 to the Song.2.7 adjuration close was considered: the same first-person speaker configuration continues at byte tier past this span's own closing seam (חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי וּפִרְי֖וֹ מָת֥וֹק לְחִכִּֽי at oshb:Song.2.3 running into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית הַיָּ֔יִן וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה at oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte, both sides), so the boundary here is not a voice-shift. It is rejected as the unit's own close because Song.2.4-Song.2.6 carries no antiphonal address-marker at all -- no vocative, no rayati/dodi term, no gendered second-person form -- while this span's own bracket is built entirely from the mirrored hinnakh/hinnekha and rayati/dodi address pairs that close formally at Song.2.2-Song.2.3; folding the two would merge a marked antiphon with an unmarked reminiscence passage under one dialogue_exchange label.

The unit closes on the embrace colon quoted from the bytes rather than in translation: וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte, 'and his right hand embraces me'), attested in that witness as “His right hand embraces me.” (web:Song.2.6), immediately before the adjuration formula breaks in at Song.2.7.

The unit closes on “Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.” (web:Song.2.17).

boundary_rationale: This unit is a narrated first-person event chain rather than pure address, anchored by the she-ahavah-nafshi formula: שֶׁאָהֲבָ֖ה נַפְשִׁ֑י (oshb:Song.3.1, tier: byte) collates byte-identical at oshb:Song.3.2 and oshb:Song.3.4, and accent_stripped at oshb:Song.3.3 (attested there as שֶׁאָהֲבָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י) -- a 5-verse skeleton-tier formula book-wide, four sites standing in this span and a fifth outside it. The narrated spine is carried by suffix-conjugation frame verbs: בִּקַּ֕שְׁתִּי (oshb:Song.3.1, tier: byte, 'I sought'), מְצָא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte, 'they found me'), and אֲחַזְתִּיו֙ (oshb:Song.3.4, tier: byte, 'I held him'), around which the rising, going-about and seeking stand as prefix-conjugation volitive shapes -- אָק֨וּמָה נָּ֜א וַאֲסוֹבְבָ֣ה ... אֲבַקְשָׁ֕ה (oshb:Song.3.2, tier: byte) -- and the not-letting-go as a further prefix-conjugation form, אַרְפֶּ֔נּוּ (oshb:Song.3.4, tier: byte). The watchmen line is quoted second-person-plural address inside the episode: רְאִיתֶֽם (oshb:Song.3.3, tier: byte, 'have you seen'). This narrated spine, not the formula alone, closes when the adjuration formula breaks in at Song.3.5.
